body.statement: If \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=r\), \(Q_{tt}\) is invertible, \(W_t=QP_t^{\mathsf T}Q_{tt}^{-1}\), and \(N=N^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{range}(N)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)\), then \(N=W_t(P_tNP_t^{\mathsf T})W_t^{\mathsf T}\).
body.justification: The lemma upgrades target-block diagonalization to an identity for every full covariance shift.
body.gap: BACKSHIFT and coroICA use global diagonalizers; neither isolates the coordinate-restriction inverse needed for a labeled principal-block converse.
body.consumer: The positive-noise realization theorem uses this identity to reconstruct every full shift from its target block.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{range}(Q)\) and \(K=QP_t^{\mathsf T}\).  Since \(P_tK=Q_{tt}\) is invertible, the \(r\) columns of \(K\) are linearly independent.  The rank assumption \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=r\) therefore gives \(\operatorname{range}(K)=\mathcal S\).  Moreover,
\[
 P_tW_t=P_tQP_t^{\mathsf T}Q_{tt}^{-1}=I_r,
 \qquad \operatorname{range}(W_t)\subseteq\mathcal S.
\]
Thus \(W_t\) is the inverse of the restriction \(P_t\vert_{\mathcal S}:\mathcal S\to\mathbb R^r\), and consequently
\[
 W_tP_tx=x\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal S. \tag{1}
\]
Every column of \(N\) belongs to \(\mathcal S\) by the stated range condition, so (1), applied columnwise, gives \(W_tP_tN=N\).  Since \(N=N^{\mathsf T}\), transposing this equality gives \(NP_t^{\mathsf T}W_t^{\mathsf T}=N\).  Hence
\[
 W_t(P_tNP_t^{\mathsf T})W_t^{\mathsf T}
 =(W_tP_tN)P_t^{\mathsf T}W_t^{\mathsf T}
 =NP_t^{\mathsf T}W_t^{\mathsf T}=N,
\]
which proves the claim.  No positivity condition on \(N\) was used.
